text:
maria: FYI we have an escalation from Acme re: missing day in their usage CSV for 2026-03-08 (they're in CDT). Billing shows $4.2k less than expected.
olivia: Which export did they pull? raw or daily rollup?
maria: raw_usage_export_shard_3.csv via the /exports/raw API. They attached a small sample.
maria: ```\ndate,timestamp,user_id,tokens\n2026-03-07,2026-03-07T23:50:00-05:00,u123,120\n2026-03-08,2026-03-08T01:30:00-05:00,u123,300\n2026-03-08,2026-03-08T01:30:00-05:00,u123,0\n2026-03-09,2026-03-09T00:05:00-05:00,u123,140\n```\n(Notice 2026-03-08 looks like an hour fold / duplication and a zero-row)
mike: Looks like the export retained local TZ offsets and we ran a backfill job the same morning that used the local timezone when computing partition keys.
usage-bot: Backfill job #987 started at 2026-03-08T02:15:12-05:00 (node: export-4)
mike: The dedupe key in the backfill pipeline is (user_id, date) where date = timestamp at local timezone. On DST start day (23-hour day) the fold/shifting logic resulted in the midnight bucket for 03-08 being empty for some shards.
devon: Repro steps I used: 1) set local TZ to America/Chicago on an exporter VM 2) rerun the raw export for 2026-03-08 3) observe that some rows are shifted by -1h and aggregation code groups them under 2026-03-07 or gets ignored.
maria: Customer says dashboard shows tokens for 03-07 and 03-09 but invoice shows 0 tokens for 03-08 — leads to invoice delta.
olivia: Can you confirm whether the storage layer has the original UTC timestamps? If not, we need to patch export to write UTC.
mike: Quick check: S3 objects have filenames with UTC, but CSV content has timestamp formatted via strftime with local tz. Exporter code path: exports/formatter.py line ~214 uses datetime.now(tzinfo).strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z') without normalizing to UTC.

mike: Immediate mitigation: change exporter to always call .astimezone(timezone.utc) before formatting. I'll push a hotfix to the export service and set a feature flag to re-export when timezone=utc.

olivia: Action items:
- Prepare pro-rated credit note for Acme (I'll draft). :pencil2:
- Mike to patch and queue idempotent re-export/backfill.\n- Devon to run a verification check across all DST regions for the last 5 years to estimate affected customers.

devon: I ran a quick query: ~120 orgs have exports in Americas timezones around DST boundaries in past 2 years. Probably <1% impacted but needs audit.
maria: Customer-facing note: apologize, explaining we're re-running a controlled backfill and will issue a credit if their invoice is affected. ETA 48 hours.
usage-bot: Backfill job #987 status: partial-success (20/32 shards). Failed shards: 10 (timeout), 2 (duplicate key conflict)
mike: For the backfill we need shard-locking and idempotent writes. Current backfill writes directly to daily_rollups with upsert=false which caused rows to be skipped on conflict. I'll flip to upsert and add a deterministic sort on timestamp to prefer non-zero token rows.

olivia: I'll own communications. Maria pls send the customer-safe sample CSV that shows the gap. Maria: done, sent.
maria: Next steps: patch -> re-export -> verify with OLAP query -> credit if invoice delta confirmed. Tagging SRE to monitor export latency during re-run. :eyes:

olivia: Also opening a billing incident ticket and linking to the account: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-4621
mike: I'll schedule a small maintenance window for the re-export to avoid contending with live aggregation.

olivia: Thanks team. Keep updates here, thread will be our source of truth for the customer comms. :+1:
